question.problem: If $\textrm E[X] = 4$ and $\textrm E[X^2] = 21,$ then what is $\textrm{Var}[X]?$
question.worked_solution:
We can compute the variance of a discrete random variable $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm E[X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2
$$

Substituting the given values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =21-{4}^{2} \\  & =21-16 \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$
